office_does: The District Court 1 judge, the court's only judge, hears misdemeanor and gross-misdemeanor criminal cases, traffic infractions, small claims, civil cases and protection-order petitions for central and eastern Clallam County, including Port Angeles and Sequim, and sets bail and release conditions; elected by District Court 1 voters to a four-year term.
race_blurb: Open seat after Judge David Neupert's retirement. Alex Schodowski, the court's judge pro tem since 2016 and Neupert's choice, faces deputy prosecutor Patrick David Murphy, who says the court needs a new direction and stricter release conditions for violent offenses. No bar rating was found.

candidates.summary: Clallam County District Court 1 judge pro tem since 2016 and Superior Court commissioner since 2019; a former Clallam deputy prosecutor now in private defense and personal-injury practice in Port Townsend.
highlights: District Court 1 judge pro tem since 2016; Superior Court commissioner since 2019 [S1][S3]
Former Clallam County deputy prosecutor; now a defense and personal-injury lawyer [S2][S4]
Would continue the Mental Health Court and Veterans Court [S2][S3]
On release: the law requires the least restrictive alternative, without disregarding public safety [S4]
Endorsed by retiring Judge David Neupert and District Court 2 Judge Bruce Hanify [S2][S3]

experience.basis: Not the incumbent, but about ten years as the court's pro tem judge plus a superior court commissionership, endorsed by the retiring judge, running on continuity and readiness.

safety.basis: Formation spans five-plus years of prosecution and a defense practice; she cites the least-restrictive-alternative release standard and backs therapeutic courts while listing community safety as a priority.

candidates.summary: Clallam County deputy prosecuting attorney since 2019, practicing mainly in District Court 1, after five years of private practice in Kitsap County; has no judicial service.
highlights: Deputy prosecutor in District Court 1 since 2019; reports 3,000+ cases and 75+ jury trials [S1][S2]
Says release conditions for violent offenses have been insufficient [S6][S7]
Pairs accountability with restorative justice and therapeutic courts that sanction violations [S1][S3]
Wants the court to apply public-defender eligibility rules strictly [S7]
Endorsed by retired Sheriff Bill Benedict and retired law-enforcement officers [S5]

experience.basis: No judicial service; runs explicitly on a 'new, more effective direction' for the court, against the outgoing judge's pick.

safety.basis: Career District Court prosecutor who repeatedly calls for firmer release conditions and bail for violent offenses and a victims-first approach, while also backing restorative justice and therapeutic courts.
